expository.title: Expository assistant
expository.subtitle: 5-pass pipeline (panorama → macro → micro → preachable → fidelity) that distinguishes exegetical division from preachable division.

setup.title: Configure the analysis
setup.subtitle: Define what you'll preach. The assistant analyzes the original text and proposes pericopes following its syntax, not the chapters imposed by the translation.
setup.twoTierHint: Useful when preaching a long book like Genesis, Acts, Isaiah, Jeremiah or Psalms. The assistant first splits the book into 2 to 5 major thematic sections, then divides each section into pericopes. Result: a clearer structure for long series.
setup.strictLabel: Strict mode (when exegesis is already done)
setup.strictHint: Turn this on when you already have exegetical papers ready for each unit. The assistant pauses after detecting the units so you can confirm one by one that the exegesis is done. Only then does it generate the sermon proposals in authoritative tone instead of tentative.
setup.translationNote: Analysis runs on the original biblical text: Greek (SBLGNT) for the New Testament, Hebrew (WLC) for the Old. If we can't load the original, we fall back to a translation (RVR1960 or ASV) and let you know.
setup.methodologyButtonHint: Learn the homiletical methodology behind this assistant

scope.modePassageHint: Chapter, chapter range, or verse range (including cross-chapter)
scope.passageHelper: Accepts chapters, ranges, and verse spans that cross chapters. Follows the divisions of the original language, not those imposed by the translation.
scope.minVersesError: The passage must contain at least {{min}} verses to justify the analysis.

problem.title: From text to sermon without betraying the author
problem.intro: Planning an expository series requires crossing a hard bridge: moving from biblical text syntax to a sermon the congregation can actually receive.
problem.outro: The most common trap is jumping straight from text to homiletical outline without passing through the author's argumentative logic. This assistant walks you step by step through a methodology that keeps each level distinct.

levels.title: Three levels that are NOT the same
levels.intro: Confusing these levels is the most common cause of sermons that sound biblical but don't say what the text says. The pipeline keeps them separate:

items.label: Exegetical
items.desc: follows the author's syntax and literary markers.

items.label: Argumentative
items.desc: identifies the function of each block within the book.

items.label: Preachable
items.desc: decides what gets preached alone, what combines, and what splits.

pipeline.title: Five cascading phases
pipeline.intro: Each phase attacks a different level of the problem, in order:

items.label: Panorama
items.desc: identifies genre, purpose, and pastoral problem.

items.label: Macrostructure
items.desc: divides the book into its large blocks.

items.label: Microstructure
items.desc: finds exegetical units with genre-specific criteria (participial chains for Greek epistle, waw-consecutive for Hebrew narrative, parallelism for poetry).

items.label: Preachable conversion
items.desc: decides how each unit becomes a sermon.

items.label: Fidelity review
items.desc: audits the proposal before you create the series.

output.title: Two propositions per unit, not one
output.intro: Each preachable unit carries two complementary hypotheses:

items.label: Exegetical hypothesis
items.desc: what the author does in the text.

items.label: Homiletical line
items.desc: how the listener receives the truth.

output.outro: Keeping them separate prevents the sermon from leaping to application without first explaining the text. They are initial hypotheses — final validation is your work with the detailed exegetical paper.

original.title: Original text when available
original.intro: The assistant cites syntactic markers directly from the original when available:

items.label: SBLGNT
items.desc: Greek text for the New Testament.

items.label: WLC
items.desc: Westminster Leningrad Codex for Old Testament Hebrew.

original.outro: If the download fails over network or the book isn't in the source, we fall back to translation (RVR1960/ASV) and notify you — analysis continues, with transparency that it's approximate.

heritage.title: A methodology with seminary lineage
heritage.intro: The pipeline draws from the historical homiletical tradition:

items.label: Sidney Greidanus
items.desc: The Modern Preacher and the Ancient Text.

heritage.outro: It does not replace your exegetical work: it accelerates it. The structure, phase names, and genre-specific criteria all come directly from this tradition.

preachable.preliminaryBanner: These are initial homiletical hypotheses based on a panoramic reading of the text. Refine them after detailed exegetical study ("Create paper from unit" in the series detail). The fields are editable — adjust title, hypothesis, homiletical line and objective at your discretion before creating the series.
preachable.strictBanner: Strict mode: every unit was confirmed with an accepted exegetical paper. Propositions reflect validated exegesis and are written in authoritative voice.
